reason: Intended difference (RDD finding A): --mask is documented to redact user identities, but Python mask() only masks role-less base64-like runs of 16+ characters, so user names (jdoe, admin, guest, station, root, the 'bad' login attempt) printed in clear. Go applies allowlist masking (rule v3): only operation names and slot paths print under --mask; everything else in an audit section is masked. A section is an audit section when the schema has an 'operation' field or an AuditRecord record type, or when it holds a writeUTF AuditEvent operation name. In it a printable run overlapping a framed record's userName (or, for Login/Login Failure/Logout/Logout (Timeout), its slotName, oldValue, value or non-slot-path target) prints <USER-MASKED>; a run that is exactly an operation name, or starts at the first byte of a framed record's slot-path target and ends inside it, prints verbatim; every other run prints <VALUE-MASKED>, role accounts included. stdout below is the corrected expectation; the Python capture in stdout is unchanged.
